item.title: Man dies in Christmas Day collision between car and e-scooter
item.description: A man has died following a road traffic collision involving a car and an e-scooter in Waterford city on Christmas Day. The crash happened at the junction of Manor Hill, and Hennessy’s Road at around 11:00 am. The e-scooter rider, a man in his 40s, was taken to University Hospital Waterford where he was later pronounced dead. item.title: Community group calls for 'masterplan' to be developed for Ballymahon
item.description: A community group in Ballymahon is calling for a 'masterplan' to be developed for the town. The Ballymahon Community Information Partnership says there are still concerns regarding public realm works. The group has organised a number of public meetings in recent months to allow residents and retailers to have their say. item.title: Leitrim Fire Service issues warning on use of extension leads over festive season
item.description: Leitrim Fire Service is warning people of the danger of using extension leads over the festive period. They're normally used more at this time of the year. People often have new electronic devices and Christmas lights also need power. Martin Bond is the senior assistant chief fire officer in Leitrim - he says caution is needed: Advertisement

item.title: Longford Women's Link says support is available over Christmas
item.description: Longford Women's Link says support is available for those who need it this Christmas. The organisation says this time of year can be the most difficult for women suffering domestic abuse. The women's link recently ran a 16-day campaign of action to oppose violence against women. It says there's usually an increase in those seeking support during the festive period. CEO Tara Farrell says Christmas can be a very worrying time, but Longford Women's Link are here to help: Advertisement

item.title: Local communities advised to stay safe and well this Christmas season
item.description: Local communities are being advised to stay safe and well this Christmas season. Cold weather can pose significant risks for people aged 65 and over, who are more vulnerable to hypothermia, falls, respiratory illnesses and complications from chronic medical conditions. A number of supports are also available to those who feel vulnerable this time of year. Aisling Dunne, local community safety co-ordinator has this advice: Advertisement
